Subject: Technical alignment: throughput & latency playbook for Cobalt Diagnostics

Hi Reena / Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Pain & goals (what we heard)
- Real-time triage assistant needs p95 latency <= 150ms at peak (conservative target), sustained throughput ~250 req/s for 512-token requests.
- Data residency: PHI must remain in your VPC for inference paths.
- Model fidelity: want to run an internal fine-tuned Llama-variant (7B/13B) with occasional fallback to a quantized 6-bit variant for cost spikes.
- Auditability: detailed token-level logs for regulated workflows (retain 90 days).

Technical constraints called out on the call
- TTL for cached prefixes ~30m for repeated patient prompts.
- KV cache size budget per GPU: ~22GB effective after quantized weights.
- Concurrency: average concurrent sessions estimated 60–80; burst to 150 for scheduled shift changes.

Redwood's recommended initial plan (short):
1) Private deployment in your AWS account (VPC connector) to satisfy data residency; Dedicated pool with mixed instance types (A100-style for peak, 80GB Vram equivalents for large KV).
2) Baseline SLOs: p50 60ms, p95 140ms for 512 tokens; throttling policy at 180ms to route to pre-warmed quantized fallback.
3) KV prefix caching + per-customer cache namespace — reduces token compute by ~18–28% for your workload profile.
4) Autoscaling policy tuned for queue depth rather than simple CPU/GPU util — better for tail latency control.

Attachments I’m including: a short playbook (redwood_playbook_throughput-latency.pdf) and a topology sketch (topology-sketch-v2.png) that maps where the cache, routing, and audit logs live. Also a quick CSV for suggested KV cache sizing.

Next steps / asks
- Jordan (cc) to follow up with a technical checklist and a prioritized test plan (sandbox access + 48h perf run).
- Reena: can you share a small representative prompt set (anonymized) and expected concurrent session cadence for a weekday peak?
- Sam: are there procurement or compliance checkpoints we should anticipate for Private deployment (KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2 evidence)?

If that looks right I’ll draft a short statement of work for the pilot (4-week sandbox + 2-week perf validation).

Thanks,
Marcus

- Our 512-token estimate is a median; longer notes (1k tokens) happen ~8% of the time — important for capacity planning.

Hi Reena / Sam —

Quick answers to the fallback & hallucination question, plus proposed perf test plan: 

Fallback and fidelity
- Quantized fallback is configured as a compatible model variant (same architecture, lower-precision weights). We recommend the following guardrails:
  - Token-level log comparison on a small representative eval set (we’ll compute divergence metrics).
  - Soft-routing threshold based on response quality signals (e.g., grep for domain-specific hallucination patterns) before failing over entirely.
  - Canary rollout: route 5% of traffic to the quantized variant and run A/B evals for 24–48h before widening.
- Rollback: automatic rollback policy if hallucination metrics exceed the accepted delta (we will define delta together). Rollback occurs at the routing layer and preserves live sessions by rerouting new requests to the primary model while completing in-flight quantized responses.

Performance test plan (sandbox)
- 48h workload run with mixed request sizes (50% 512 tokens, 8% 1k tokens, rest short). 
- Measure p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end request (including pre/post-processing) and token-generation. 
- KV-cache effectiveness test: re-run a subset of prompts with cache enabled/disabled to measure delta.

Deliverables (what we’ll hand back)
- Perf report (csv + dashboard link), hallucination divergence report, and a short ops-runbook for autoscaling thresholds.

I’ll attach a lightweight test harness and schedule the perf run once we have the sample prompts and sandbox credentials.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Blake
